About the show

Which role undid you in the end?

Electra. A daughter consumed by grief and rage, clinging to the idea of justice as her world comes apart.

Persona. During a performance of Electra, an actress suddenly falls silent. What follows is a rupture: two women drawn into an intense, unsettling encounter where speech breaks down and the boundaries between self and role give way.

Featuring Cate Blanchett (The Seagull), Nina Hoss (The Cherry Orchard), and Ella Lily Hyland (Black Doves), Benedict Andrews’ (A Streetcar Named Desire) thrilling production fuses ancient myth and modern psychology in a powerful exploration of identity, and the fragile line between who we are and who we play.

Book official tickets for Electra/Persona, the new play by Benedict Andrews featuring Cate Blanchett and Nina Hoss. Playing in the Lyttelton Theatre at the National Theatre in London, from Wednesday 19 August to Saturday 10 October 2026.

Suitability

Please note: this production contains descriptions and depictions of a sexual nature, violence and murder. References and description of suicide. This production contains flashing lights, loud sounds and haze.

The production is supported by ME+EM and Laura Bickford & Stephen Graham.

Assisted performances

The National Theatre offers a range of accessible theatre performances for Electra/Persona, to support Deaf, disabled and neurodivergent audiences, as well as anyone who may benefit from additional access support when attending this stage production in London.

Explore accessible performances for Electra/Persona below:

Captioned

Captioned performances have text on screens so that deaf and hard of hearing, or anyone that would like to read along, can also enjoy the performance.
Thursday 10 September – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona
Wednesday 30 September – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona

BSL Interpreted

There will be a trained British Signed Language (BSL) interpreter, usually standing to one side of the stage, interpreting the script used by the performers at the same time as it is being performed.
Friday 18 September – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona
Thursday 1 October – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona

Audio described

Audio description is a live commentary interspersed with the actors' dialogue. This is relayed via a headset.
Saturday 12 September – 1pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona
Thursday 8 October – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona

No Chilled performance available.

No Dementia-friendly performances available.

Relaxed performance

Technical changes are made to the production, such as adjustments to light and sound effects, for those with sensory sensitivities. These performances also allow for noise and movement in the auditorium, a chill-out space for patrons who may need time away from the performance, and re-entry when needed.
Wednesday 7 October – 7pm
Book Tickets for Electra/Persona

The interpreter for the BSL performance will be Becky Barry. The BSL Consultant is Sophie Stone.

Audio-described performances are preceded by a Touch Tour, 90 minutes before the performance start time. Call the Access line on 020 7452 3961 to book Touch Tours.

The Audio describers will be Miranda Yates and Jenny Stewart-Cosgrove.

We have an allocation of tickets held for members of our Access scheme and if any of the assisted performances above are shown as “Sold Out”, tickets may still be available: Please log in to your account to view all available tickets, or call Box Office on 020 7452 3961
